payload.text: **THE OUTCOME ROW, AND IT IS THE ONLY ONE THAT ANSWERS THE ORIGINAL QUESTION.** A full suite run, INCLUDING one deliberately interrupted mid-flight, leaves zero `intentd` processes that were not running before it started. Counted by matching the EXECUTABLE -- `ps -axo pid=,command=` with the argv[0] field, never `pgrep -f`, **which is unsound in BOTH directions**: it matches command-line text, so it counts observers and any process merely mentioning the name, and it can also miss a long command line. Its count is neither a floor nor a ceiling. **The direction is load-bearing rather than pedantic, and this row's first wording had it backwards.** It said `pgrep -f` UNDER-reports, on a 64-against-67 reading whose 67 was itself the over-count. AC-05.1 is a ZERO claim, so a reader told only that the instrument under-reports treats its count as a FLOOR -- and at a true population of zero it can read non-zero, which makes a satisfied row look unsatisfiable. (ic drove the over-count, 4 true against 7 from `pgrep -f`, the three extras being a peer's shell wrapper and this measurement's own subshells; the wording is theirs.) **Every other row here is a mechanism; this one is the estate.** Evidence: the before/after counts and the interruption method, recorded on this thread.
